newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hitachi, Toshiba mull Asia nuclear plant tie-ups.
newsitem.headline: Hitachi, Toshiba mull Asia nuclear plant tie-ups.

text.p: Japanese electric machinery makers Hitachi Ltd and Toshiba Corp said on Monday they are considering jointly seeking contracts for nuclear power plant projects in Asia.
The two firms have close ties in the domestic market as both specialise in boiling water reactors (BWR), a Hitachi spokesman said.
The other major Japanese electric machinery manufacturer, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd, builds pressurised water reactors.

Hitachi and Toshiba, as members of a consortium led by General Electric Co, won a 180 billion yen ($1.59 billion) contract earlier this year from Taiwan to build two advanced boiling water reactors, marking Japan's first power reactor export.

Japanese nuclear plant manufacturers are keen to break into booming Asian markets as construction of nuclear plants has become increasingly difficult in Japan following a coolant leakage at an experimental reactor a year ago.
Three tonnes of sodium coolant leaked from a fast-breeder nuclear reactor in December last year, undermining public confidence in the safety of nuclear power plants. ($1=113 yen)
